milestoneContract.title: V6 PKG-T2 orchestrator executor integration tests against real git
milestoneContract.objective: Exercise the unattended orchestrator's real executors against real temporary git repositories, with every non-git process faked and recorded, so merge, adoption, signing, Phase0 and builder-round safety properties are proven before activation, without touching protected files or any pending package scope.
requirements: [V6-PKG-T2-ORCHESTRATOR-EXECUTOR-INTEGRATION-2026-09-29 founderAuthorization.rule] Founder rule 2026-09-29: A blocked/review-pending package blocks ONLY its own dependency lane. While a package waits for Codex/review/provider availability, preserve its exact frozen review scope, do not modify its branch, frozen bundle, review clone, evidence or review-cycle state, do not merge it before the required CLEAN review, and immediately implement the next independent eligible package in an isolated branch, validate, checkpoint, commit, prepare the frozen review bundle, mark it REVIEW_PENDING if Codex is unavailable, and continue.
[V6-PKG-T2-ORCHESTRATOR-EXECUTOR-INTEGRATION-2026-09-29 founderAuthorization.constraint] Tests and non-protected documentation only; no protected file, no pending package scope, no merge.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical validation (config/validation.json) passes on the exact reviewed commit on Windows with Node >=24 and npm >=11, and the checkpoint records the measured validation environment.
The selftest uses real git for git contracts and records every other process without executing it; no scenario reaches a real provider, network, signing key or installation.

Each scenario asserts a real safety property of the unchanged executors: fast-forward-only merge bound to matching CLEAN evidence, adoption without provider or script calls, public-key-only signing and signer waits, Phase0 ZIP hash/remote/failed-attempt guards, builder-round rejection of out-of-scope, unauthorized protected and trust-manifest edits without moving the branch.
No protected file changes, the trust-root manifest is unchanged, and no existing test, validator or policy is weakened.
mandatoryFailureCases: a scenario that passes without asserting its property
a real provider, signing or install process spawned by the tests
a protected file or pending package scope changed
